name: Product Line Optimization Agent
headline: Find the constraint before it becomes the production plan
pitch: Turn line efficiency, station cycle time, quality, and shift data into an operating view that exposes bottlenecks, compares improvement paths, and gives plant leaders a practical plan for protecting throughput and quality.
why_try: It makes operational AI concrete: a plant manager can ask where output is being lost, see the constraining station, and evaluate process, equipment, quality, or staffing responses.
customer_challenge: A manufacturer facing demand pressure lacks one shared view of line performance. Bottlenecks, shift constraints, and defect patterns are reviewed manually, making it harder to respond without trading away quality.
microsoft_ai_story: Microsoft Copilot Studio provides the natural-language experience. Dynamics 365 ERP contributes production and resource context, Azure IoT Hub supplies equipment signals, and Power BI presents line health and improvement scenarios.
business_value: Improves visibility into where capacity and quality are being lost across production lines.
Accelerates bottleneck analysis and turns operational signals into targeted improvement options.
Strengthens shift planning and investment decisions while keeping quality and disruption risk visible.

capabilities.name: Line health overview
capabilities.purpose: Combines availability, performance, quality, and output context to show where operating attention is needed.

capabilities.name: Station-level constraint analysis
capabilities.purpose: Compares cycle time with takt time and quality signals to identify the station constraining each line.

capabilities.name: Improvement option planning
capabilities.purpose: Frames process, equipment, and quality interventions so plant leaders can compare practical response paths.

capabilities.name: Shift production planning
capabilities.purpose: Translates line performance and staffing context into a shift-level operating plan.

prompts.label: See which production line needs attention
prompts.prompt: Which production line needs attention today, and what is driving the loss?

recorded_answer.prompt: Which production line needs attention today, and what is driving the loss?
recorded_answer.answer:
Biggest concern today: **Polymer Molding Line C** — it has the lowest OEE (68%) and the largest output gap (1,728 units/day lost), plus the highest annual quality cost ($352,800).

What's driving it:
- **Availability is the main culprit** — only 78%, well below the others, meaning more downtime/stoppages than any other line.
- Performance (89.7%) and quality (97.2%) are actually decent, so this isn't a speed or defect problem — it's a *reliability/uptime* problem (changeovers, breakdowns, or stoppages).

Worth noting: Electronics Assembly Line A and Production Line 3 are also both below target OEE (70.9%), driven more by performance losses (82%) than availability. But Line C is the one bleeding the most output and dollars right now.

Want me to pull the bottleneck analysis for Line C to see exactly which station is causing the downtime?

prompts.label: Find the constraining station
prompts.prompt: Where is the bottleneck on each line, and which station should the plant team address first?

recorded_answer.prompt: Where is the bottleneck on each line, and which station should the plant team address first?
recorded_answer.answer:
Here's the bottleneck on each line:

- **Line 3** – SMT Placement Station 3B: +37.4% over takt (worst overage on the plant)
- **Line A** – Functional Test: +26.5% over takt
- **Line B** – Robotic Welding: +18.3% over takt
- **Line C** – Injection Molding: +22.7% over takt, also the highest defect rate (0.45%)

**Address first: SMT Placement Station 3B on Line 3.** It has the largest takt overage of any station plant-wide, and with Line 3's 40% holiday surge demand coming, it'll constrain throughput the hardest if left unaddressed. Injection Molding on Line C is a close second priority given its defect rate is driving quality losses.

Want the optimization plan for Line 3's bottleneck?

prompts.label: Compare throughput improvement options
prompts.prompt: Give me the practical options to improve throughput without hiding the quality tradeoffs.

recorded_answer.prompt: Give me the practical options to improve throughput without hiding the quality tradeoffs.
recorded_answer.answer:
Here's the throughput picture across all four lines, each with a real quality angle:

**Line 3** (gap 20 uph): cycle-time cut on SMT Station 3B is cheapest (+12 uph, process/tooling only), parallel station adds +17 uph but costs $45K–$120K, quality fix on the same station only buys +4 uph — tradeoff: cycle-time cuts push the bottleneck harder, which is exactly where the 0.1% defect already lives, so squeezing speed without the quality fix risks defect rate creeping up.

**Line A** (gap 38 uph): same pattern — Functional Test cycle-time cut (+23) or parallel unit (+32, $45K–$120K). The real defect risk is downstream at Final Assembly (0.18%), not at the station you'd be speeding up, so there's less direct tension here.

**Line B** (gap 39 uph): Robotic Welding is both the bottleneck and the defect hotspot (0.3%, highest of the four). Cycle-time cut or parallel station speeds up the exact process generating defects — this is the one where "faster" and "lower quality" are most likely to collide.

**Line C** (gap 72 uph, biggest gap): Injection Molding cuts give the largest raw gains (+43 to +61 uph) but it's also running the highest defect rate (0.45%). Chasing throughput here without the quality option risks the worst scrap/rework blowback of the four lines.

Bottom line: parallel-station options buy the most uph but cost real money ($45K–$120K) and don't fix defects; cycle-time cuts are cheaper but stress the bottleneck station, which is often also the defect source — worst on Line B and Line C. Want the full financial/ROI breakdown for any one line?

prompts.label: Build the three-shift production plan
prompts.prompt: Translate the current line performance into a day, swing, and night shift plan.

recorded_answer.prompt: Translate the current line performance into a day, swing, and night shift plan.
recorded_answer.answer:
Here's the shift plan across all four lines, built on current performance data:

**Schedule:** Day (6a–2p, 24 ops), Swing (2p–10p, 22 ops), Night (10p–6a, 18 ops, +15% premium pay)

**Daily output split evenly across all 3 shifts per line:**
- Line 3: 800/800/800 = 2,400/day
- Line A: 1,136/1,136/1,136 = 3,408/day
- Line B: 2,088/2,088/2,088 = 6,264/day
- Line C: 1,344/1,344/1,344 = 4,032/day

**Line 3 holiday surge note:** adding a 4th overlap shift with 12 extra operators adds +400 units/day — key lever for hitting the 40% surge target.

**Weekly capacity** scales cleanly at 5/6/7-day operation (e.g., Line 3 hits 16,800/week at 7 days).

Want me to layer in the Line 3 bottleneck fixes to see how they shift these per-shift numbers?
